subject: Urgent: AtlasFusion throughput collapse — network path triage & exec sync
body:
From: Sara McKenna <sara@atlasfusion.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: AtlasFusion Ops <ops@atlasfusion.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jan 2029 08:23:00 -0800
Subject: Production throughput collapse — Redwood inference calls failing at scale

Neha,

We started seeing a sharp throughput collapse at 07:55 PST. Traffic to your hosted endpoint for model: rdx-large-24 is dropping from ~800 RPS to ~40 RPS and TCP latencies spike to 1.2s end-to-end. Partial 5xx errors (gateway timeouts) are appearing and retries are compounding the queue. This is impacting our checkout flow.

Attached are a sample of request traces and a Grafana screenshot. Our SREs see long socket connect times and repeated DNS resolution delays to the Redwood ingress hostname (resolves intermittently to different AZ IPs). Can you confirm whether there are any peering or egress changes on your side? We need a timeline and immediate mitigations — our leadership is asking for an exec-level incident update.

--
Sara McKenna
Head of Platform, AtlasFusion
Sara.McKenna@atlasfusion.com


-----Original Message-----
(attachments: latency-samples.csv, trace-graph.png)

----
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Sara McKenna <sara@atlasfusion.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Jan 2029 08:41:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Production throughput collapse — Redwood inference calls failing at scale

Sara — thanks for the data, and sorry for the impact. We’ve triaged at a high level and are pursuing two parallel hypotheses: 1) transient DNS resolution instability in one of our egress regions causing connection amplification, and 2) a proxy health flap in front of the dedicated pool serving AtlasFusion (causing sticky connections to drain).

Immediate actions taken:
- I’ve asked infra to pin AtlasFusion traffic to the alternate egress cluster and enable bypass routing (T=08:39).
- Ben is running targeted connection captures on the dedicated pool (Ben: latest pcap attached to the internal incident room).
- Rishi is opening a peering/route validation with the cloud provider to check VPC path anomalies.

We’ll follow up with a short exec-ready summary in 45 minutes. Do you have an ETA target you need from us for the leadership update?

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai


----
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Jan 2029 09:05:37 -0800
Subject: RE: Production throughput collapse — Redwood inference calls failing at scale

Neha / team — quick notes from the pool: we see TCP SYN retries concentrated against the egress NAT in us-west-2 cluster A; the proxy in front of the pool (hp-proxy-12) is cycling health checks and marking backends out for 30-45s before re-registering. DNS resolution times for api.redwood.example occasionally spike to ~700ms per query from our edge nodes — but resolution does eventually return different A-records across AZs.

I have a temporary mitigation toggled: aggressive keepalive and reduced idle timeout for the proxy + increase in connection pool size for AtlasFusion route (applied 08:53). Early telemetry shows some improvement in request throughput to ~300 RPS but latency still high for some buckets. I’ve attached summarized packet captures.

(attachment stub: internal-pool-pcap-01.pcap)

-ben
Ben Carter
Lead Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai


----
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Jan 2029 10:18:22 -0800
Subject: RE: Production throughput collapse — Redwood inference calls failing at scale

All — I opened an immediate support case with the cloud provider and escalated to peering/network ops. Initial reply indicates an intermittent BGP flap on one of our transit peers in us-west-2 between 07:45–08:12 which would cause DNS resolvers aggregated in that region to see inconsistent answers and route churn.

Actions we’re coordinating now:
- Ask cloud provider to reroute DNS queries to secondary resolvers for the impacted AZs (in flight).
- Shift AtlasFusion tenant to alternate dedicated pool in us-west-2b (in progress).
- In parallel, we should prepare fallback policy to route traffic to the secondary model variant in a different region (us-west-1) if the egress instability persists beyond 30 minutes.

Given AtlasFusion leadership asking for an exec sync, I recommend Vivek join the call to provide the incident posture and customer remediation plan.

-rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai


----
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Sara McKenna <sara@atlasfusion.com>, AtlasFusion Ops <ops@atlasfusion.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jan 2029 11:02:10 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Production throughput collapse — Exec sync scheduled (11:30 PST)

Team / Sara — forwarding consolidated findings and recommended exec-level remediation steps for the 11:30 PST sync. Please see below for the short talking points; attach the two artifacts (latency-samples.csv, trace-graph.png) to the summary deck.

Executive summary (2 min):
- Impact: AtlasFusion saw ~90% throughput reduction and intermittent 502/504s between 07:45–09:30 PST. Partial recovery after proxy config changes but residual latency remains for ~10% of requests.
- Cause (probable): Transit peer BGP flap in us-west-2 causing DNS resolver inconsistency and proxy health flaps that led to connection churn.
- Mitigation applied: rerouted DNS resolvers, rotated AtlasFusion to alternate dedicated pool, proxy timeouts and keepalive tuned (applied by 09:00).
- Short-term next steps (owner): 1) Cloud provider to confirm full peering stabilization (Rishi/cloud), 2) Redwood to enable cross-region fallback to us-west-1 model variant (Ben/infra), 3) Ops to monitor error-rate/latency for 2 hours and report back (Neha).
- Ask of customer: Allow Redwood to enable controlled cross-region failover for AtlasFusion for the next 24 hours to fully mitigate impact and validate recovery.

Meeting: 11:30 PST, WebEx (link shared in calendar). Vivek — can you lead the opening 3 min and commitment to a follow-up RCA within 48 hours?

Thanks,
Neha


----
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Sara McKenna <sara@atlasfusion.com>, AtlasFusion Ops <ops@atlasfusion.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jan 2029 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production throughput collapse — Exec sync scheduled (11:30 PST)

Everyone — thanks for the rapid triage and the clear remediation steps. I joined the 11:30 sync and spoke with AtlasFusion leadership — they appreciated the transparency. Committed items and timelines we promised on the call:

1) Immediate: Redwood will keep cross-region failover enabled for AtlasFusion for 24 hours and monitor in 5-minute windows. Owner: Ben.
2) Near-term: Cloud provider will confirm full peering stability and provide the BGP incident log to us. Owner: Rishi (ETA 12 hours).
3) RCA: Redwood will deliver a detailed postmortem within 48 hours with root cause, timeline, and remediation preventing recurrence (Owner: Neha + Ben + Rishi).

AtlasFusion asked for a temporary service credit as a gesture for the outage impact; we acknowledged the ask and committed to follow-up after the RCA. Please collate all telemetry and attach the pcap + DNS logs to the postmortem folder (link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AtlasFusion-Incident-DF4781).

I’ll take point on the executive summary distribution. Put the RCA draft in the folder and ping me when it’s ready for review.

—
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
